slides.heading: Interview *round 1*

messages.text: STANDARD, SORTED or HASHED: which one for big lookups?
HASHED. A read by the full unique key takes the same time at any size.

slides.voiceover: Interview में पूछा गया: बड़े lookups के लिए कौन सी table? जवाब: HASHED.
slides.spoken: Interview mein poocha gaya: bade lookups ke liye kaun si table? Jawaab: HASHED.

slides.label: KEY POINT
slides.heading: *SORTED* for partial keys
slides.body: STANDARD: index access. SORTED: binary search, partial key. HASHED: full unique key only.
slides.voiceover: Partial key से पढ़ना है तो SORTED, और index चाहिए तो STANDARD.
slides.spoken: Partial key se padhna hai to SORTED, aur index chahiye to STANDARD.

posts.caption:
"STANDARD, SORTED or HASHED?" comes up in almost every ABAP interview.

1. STANDARD: index access, linear search by key. Fine for small tables and ALV output.
2. SORTED: kept sorted by its key, binary search, supports partial keys.
3. HASHED: full unique key only, constant read time at any size.

Which one do you use inside loops?
